subject: NexBridge perf follow-up: p95/p99 acceptance checklist & demo plan
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@nexbridge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: NexBridge perf follow-up: p95/p99 acceptance checklist & demo plan

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so we can progress the p95/p99 qualification for the hosted API vs your incumbent. Please flag anything I missed.

Call recap (plain):
- Goal: validate Redwood hosted will meet NexBridge end-to-end p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 320ms across typical user flows (search/autocomplete, structured chat with tool calls).
- Traffic envelope: 60–200 qps peak expected in prod; typical payloads are 80–300 tokens; 95th token length ~260. Streaming used for chat UI (server-sent events).
- Key constraints: tail latency for streaming connections, concurrency limit per session, and KV cache priming for repeated prefixes.

Proposed qualification plan (attached: nexbridge-slo-testplan-v1.pdf and traffic envelope):
1) Shadow run — 4 hours using your real traffic envelope (we'll shadow route 10% of requests to Redwood) to collect tail distributions.
2) Controlled POC — synthetic traffic with same token-length distribution: baseline (10 qps), ramp (60 qps), peak (200 qps) with both cold and primed KV cache windows.
3) Streaming concurrency probe — measure p95/p99 with 100 and 400 concurrent streaming clients to verify connection churn handling.
4) Rollout criteria: p95 <= 120ms and p99 <= 320ms for the two mission-critical routes (search, chat) and no more than 3% request error rate during load.

Immediate asks from NexBridge to start:
- Final traffic CSV (sample distribution + qps windows) — Laura can take this.
- List of endpoints and headers we should mirror for shadowing.
- A preferred 2–4 hour window next week for the shadow run (we can be flexible M–F).

Next steps / owners:
- Samir: confirm shadow window + send simplified traffic CSV (link or attach).
- Laura: prepare shadow routing snippet + temp creds.
- Karthik: will scope resource sizing and NVMe/quantization knobs based on the envelope.

Attachments: nexbridge-slo-testplan-v1.pdf (SLO matrix + test schedule), nexbridge-traffic-envelope.csv (sensitive).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20-min sync if helpful.

—
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Priya Chopra <priya.chopra@nexbridge.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@nexbridge.com>, eng@nexbridge.com
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NexBridge perf follow-up: p95/p99 acceptance checklist & demo plan

Thanks Aditya — appreciated. Quick clarifications from our side: 
- The p95/p99 targets you listed are for end-to-end (client -> our gateway -> model response). Can you confirm that includes any gateway overhead and our CDN?
- For streaming, we use chunked SSE and our frontend opens long-lived connections per user. Measuring p99 on streaming often spikes; is the 400 concurrent clients probe you mentioned per region or global?

We attached a trimmed traffic sample (trimmed-traffic.csv) and added a short note on token length distribution. Two windows that matter most for us: weekday peak (14:00–16:00 PT) and batch-night (02:00–04:00 PT) when background inference bursts.

We can do the shadow run next Tuesday 2027-07-06 14:00–18:00 PT if that works. Procurement will also want a brief summary of how fallback behavior works — if Redwood misses SLOs, what automatic fallback happens (we currently fall back to a smaller local model).

Priya
Head of Platform Engineering, NexBridge
priya.chopra@nexbridge.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Chopra <priya.chopra@nexbridge.com>, Samir Patel <samir@nexbridge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NexBridge perf follow-up: p95/p99 acceptance checklist & demo plan

Great — thanks for the sample and the windows. Quick answers inline: 
- End-to-end scope: yes, our measurements will be from your edge (the request as it reaches Redwood) through model decoding and to the final chunk delivered to the client. We'll instrument a small client-side marker if you prefer, but measuring at your gateway ingress is typical and accounts for CDN overhead pre-ingress.
- Streaming concurrency semantics: the 400 clients is global for the single region (we recommend running regionally to avoid cross-region variability). For NexBridge we'll run regionally in us-west-2 per your traffic window.

Fallback behavior: Redwood supports automated fallback policies — typical config in the attachment:
- Primary -> Redwood hosted model.
- On elevated latency/error threshold (configurable example: p99 > 500ms or error rate > 5% for 1 minute) we can failover to a pinned smaller variant (lower-cost, faster but modestly lower quality) and send an alert to NexBridge.

Confirming shadow slot: 2027-07-06 14:00–18:00 PT booked tentatively on our side (will finalize once you send the final traffic CSV). Laura — please prepare the routing snippet and a short checklist for Ops. Karthik — can you confirm if we need additional GPUs in the window or if autoscaling will cover 200 qps with the expected token mix?

—
Aditya

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Chopra <priya.chopra@nexbridge.com>, Samir Patel <samir@nexbridge.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NexBridge perf follow-up: p95/p99 acceptance checklist & demo plan

Thanks — some technical clarifications ahead of the shadow run so we can size and ensure test fidelity: 
1) Traffic fidelity: please confirm whether the CSV line items include a header with route names (search, chat, tooling) and the sample percent per route. If not, send a small mapping.
2) Auth/headers: can we get a sample request with the headers you commonly add? That lets us mirror request size and handshake overhead.
3) Long-lived connections: how many simultaneous websocket/SSE connections should we target per qps bucket (e.g., 60 qps with 1K long-lived users vs 200 qps with 3.5K)? Knowing this we can ensure connection churn and acceptor limits are realistic.
4) Error semantics: what is considered a retry on your side vs client drop? We will instrument to distinguish transient 5xx vs application-level rejections.

Operational asks: please provide a short Slack channel or escalation contact on the day of the run. We'll publish a short runbook and a dashboard link beforehand.

I'll attach the quick-sizing sheet and the test runner config — Laura, please include these in the Ops checklist.

—Karthik
Sr. Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir@nexbridge.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NexBridge perf follow-up: p95/p99 acceptance checklist & demo plan

All good — we confirm 2027-07-06 14:00–18:00 PT for the shadow run. Attaching the final traffic CSV (trimmed-traffic.csv). A couple quick points: 
- Route split: search 45%, chat 40%, background-batch 15%.
- Peak long-lived connections: estimate ~3,100 SSE clients in us-west-2 during peak.
- Auth headers: we will send a sample cURL and a short header spec to eng@nexbridge.com by Monday.

Procurement also asked that we document the SLA fallback policy for the contract — happy to get the short summary you mentioned. Otherwise please proceed with the tentative runbook and send the Ops channel.

Thanks — Samir
Director of Product | NexBridge
